reviews.quote: Asus sells the ROG Xbox Ally in just one configuration. The $599.99 model comes with an AMD Ryzen Z2 A processor, 16GB of RAM, a 512GB SSD, and a 7-inch, 1080p touchscreen.

The ROG Xbox Ally is Asus's more affordable take on its new handheld line. At €599 it goes head-to-head with Valve's Steam Deck OLED, but under the hood it still runs on AMD's older Zen 2 architecture, limiting performance gains.

praises: Cheapest way into the Xbox Fullscreen Experience — BBY owners call the console-style UI and quick resume a huge upgrade over desktop Windows at any price
C$799.99 undercuts the Steam Deck LCD (C$1,129) while running Game Pass, anti-cheat multiplayer and every PC launcher (Tom's Hardware framed it as 'the cheapest Windows handheld')
Same comfortable Xbox-grip chassis, 120Hz VRR 7" 1080p screen and hall-effect-style controls as the C$1,500 Ally X — the ergonomics carry down intact
The power-efficient 4-core Z2 A runs cool and quiet; indie/older/2D titles and cloud streaming feel effortless
Healthy retail stock and BBY open-box from $679.99 make it the low-risk entry handheld in Canada (open-box culture is a BBY theme in its 1,000+ reviews)
complaints: The Z2 A is a 4-core Zen 2 / 8-CU RDNA 2 part — modern AAA at 1080p is a slideshow even on Low; NBC's benchmark sampling (e.g. ~12 FPS averages at Ultra in Turbo) shows it well below the Steam Deck
16GB RAM at 6400MT/s (slower than the Ally X's 7467/8000) further limits the weak iGPU — heavy emulation and newer titles suffer
Same dim glossy 7" IPS panel as the rest of the line; no brightness spec published for this SKU
60Wh (vs 80Wh on both bigger siblings) despite the small APU — runtime is good only because the machine can't push hard
At C$799.99 it sits close to the C$899.97 Z1 Extreme Ally X clearance, which is dramatically faster — value math favours the older flagship (top 'which one?' objection in r/ROGAlly threads)

design_philosophy: The volume tier of the ASUS-Microsoft handheld push: an intentionally old, cheap Zen 2-based Ryzen Z2 A APU wrapped in the same Xbox-grip chassis, screen and Fullscreen Experience software as the flagship, sold at a US$599/C$799 price aimed at Game Pass families rather than handheld-PC enthusiasts. ASUS sells exactly one configuration (16GB/512GB), keeping it simple. The trade-offs are severe — 4 Zen 2 cores and an 8-CU RDNA 2 iGPU are several generations behind — but the software experience and ergonomics are identical to the Ally X.
